issue.title: [all components] Use shadow DOM-safe DOM utilities

labels.name: scope: all components
labels.description: Widespread work has an impact on almost all components.

issue.body:
This patch standardizes shadow DOM-safe DOM access across the codebase by switching affected paths to shared `contains`, `getTarget`, `activeElement`, `ownerDocument`, and `ownerWindow` patterns.

## Changes

- Add a private shadow DOM helper for the floating-ui React internals and align affected call sites with it.
- Fix cross-realm and retargeting-sensitive logic in focus, keyboard, pointer, and portal code paths.
- Update the repository guidance to require the shadow DOM-safe and owner-document/window utilities for future changes.

comments.body:
## Codex Review (GPT-5.4)

I reviewed the full branch against a freshly fetched `upstream/master`. This is a bug-fix PR with `a11y`, `react-ui`, and `tests` as relevant secondary tags; after the follow-up fix to `useButton`, I did not find any remaining blocking issues.

### 1. Bugs / Issues (None)

### 2. Root Cause & Patch Assessment

| Area | Assessment | Notes |
|------|:----------:|-------|
| Shadow DOM retargeting | Good | The diff now consistently routes the affected focus/pointer paths through shadow-DOM-safe helpers where the code needs the composed target or deepest active element. |
| Cross-realm DOM access | Good | The updated `ownerDocument` / `ownerWindow` call sites cover the realm-sensitive cases touched by this PR, including `getComputedStyle()`, portal targeting, and pointer listener registration. |
| Keyboard behavior | Good | The follow-up adjustment in `useButton` preserves React's retargeted keyboard semantics for shadow-host render targets instead of over-applying `composedPath()[0]`. |

### 3. Pattern Consistency Assessment

| Area | Status | Notes |
|------|:------:|-------|
| Shared helper usage | Consistent | The private `floating-ui-react/utils/shadowDom.ts` helper keeps the main shadow-DOM logic centralized without accidentally expanding the published `@base-ui/utils` surface. |
| Call-site updates | Consistent | The converted paths use the shadow-safe helpers only where they improve correctness, while plain `currentTarget` reads remain in place for standard input/change handling. |

### 4. Simplification Opportunities

**Strengths:**
The private helper extraction reduces duplication in `floating-ui-react/utils/element.ts` and keeps the implementation surface smaller than exporting a new top-level utils package entrypoint.

**Recommendation:**
No additional simplification changes look necessary for this branch.

### 5. Edge Cases Worth Noting

| Edge case | Status | Notes |
|-----------|:------:|-------|
| Shadow-host keyboard activation | Handled | `useButton` now keeps the pre-existing React retargeting semantics for Space/Enter behavior. |
| Nested shadow-root focus tracking | Handled | `activeElement()` continues to walk into nested shadow roots, which is important for the touched toast, drawer, slider, and number-field paths. |
| Foreign document / iframe-style ownership | Improved | The updated owner-document/window call sites should now follow the owning document more reliably in the touched code paths. |

### 6. Test Coverage Assessment

| Validation | Result | Notes |
|-----------|:------:|-------|
| `pnpm typescript` | Passed | No type regressions after the follow-up fixes. |
| `pnpm test:jsdom ToastViewport --no-watch` | Passed | Covers one of the more focus-sensitive paths touched here. |
| `pnpm test:jsdom DrawerViewport --no-watch` | Passed | Exercises the touch/focus selection logic updated in the drawer viewport. |
| `pnpm test:jsdom SliderRoot --no-watch` | Passed | Covers the slider focus/interaction path touched by the refactor. |
| `pnpm test:jsdom NumberFieldRoot --no-watch` | Passed | Passed despite the usual JSDOM `requestSubmit()` not-implemented warning during the suite. |
| `pnpm test:jsdom ScrollAreaRoot --no-watch` | Passed | Covers the pointer-target change in the scroll-area root. |
| `pnpm test:jsdom useButton --no-watch` | Passed | Validates the follow-up fix for the shadow-host keyboard regression. |

### Merge Confidence Score

| Dimension | Score | Notes |
|-----------|:-----:|-------|
| Correctness | 4/5 | I did not find a remaining correctness issue after the keyboard regression fix, but the branch touches a broad set of interaction primitives. |
| Interaction / a11y risk | 4/5 | The high-risk focus and keyboard paths were inspected directly and covered with targeted tests. |
| Maintainability | 4/5 | The helper stays private and the call-site choices are more consistent than before. |
| Validation depth | 4/5 | Typecheck plus targeted suites for the touched interaction-heavy areas all passed. |

Overall merge confidence is 4/5. I would be comfortable merging this draft once reviewers are satisfied with the broad interaction sweep.

reviews.body:
## Claude Opus 4.6 review

### Summary

This PR standardizes shadow DOM-safe DOM access across the codebase. It touches **30 files** across two commits with three categories of changes:

1. **Extract `shadowDom.ts`** — Moves `activeElement`, `contains`, and `getTarget` into a dedicated shadowDom.ts module, re-exported from element.ts.
2. **Replace `event.target` accesses** — Switches to `getTarget(event.nativeEvent)` (for React events) or `getTarget(event)` (for native events) for shadow DOM retargeting safety; also uses `event.currentTarget` where the handler's own element is the intended target.
3. **Replace bare `document`/`window`** — Uses `ownerDocument(node)` and `ownerWindow(node)` instead of global lookups for cross-realm correctness.

---

### Findings

#### Positives
- **Well-scoped and consistent.** The three utility functions (`activeElement`, `contains`, `getTarget`) are the correct primitives for shadow DOM compatibility. The refactor is methodical.
- **`event.target` → `event.currentTarget` changes are correct.** In AccordionTrigger, CheckboxRoot, NumberFieldInput, SliderThumb, SwitchRoot, SelectRoot, and AriaCombobox, the handler is reading properties from its own element (`.value`, `.checked`, `.valueAsNumber`), so `event.currentTarget` is semantically correct and simpler than `getTarget`.
- **`ownerDocument`/`ownerWindow` conversions are correct.** CalendarViewport, FloatingFocusManager, useAnchorPositioning, getPseudoElementBounds, ToastRoot, useSwipeDismiss, and usePopupViewport all correctly derive the document/window from the relevant DOM node.
- **Second commit is a good correction.** The markOthers revert from shadow-DOM `contains` back to native `parent.contains()` is correct since `markOthers` already handles shadow host unwrapping explicitly — the shadow-DOM `contains` was unnecessary there.
- **Null safety is preserved.** `ownerDocument(null)` correctly falls back to global `document`, so the `arrowRef.current || ownerDocument(arrowRef.current).createElement('div')` pattern in useAnchorPositioning is safe.
- **AGENTS.md update** correctly documents the new convention.
- **Comprehensive sweep** — no remaining bare `.activeElement` accesses; all `event.target` references in component code are either converted or are non-DOM custom events (e.g., FloatingTree's sibling menu event in MenuPositioner.tsx).
- **StoreInspector** duplicates `getTarget` locally rather than importing from the `react` package — this is correct because `StoreInspector` lives in utils which should not depend on react.

#### Issues

**Minor / Nits (non-blocking):**

1. **FloatingPortal.tsx** — `document.body` is still used as the last-resort portal container. For cross-realm correctness, this could use an element ref to derive the document, but it's an edge case (no available container or parent portal) and was not introduced by this PR.

2. **ScrollAreaScrollbar.tsx** — The change from `event.currentTarget !== event.target` to `event.currentTarget !== getTarget(event.nativeEvent)` is semantically correct for shadow DOM, but it changes the comparison semantics slightly: in shadow DOM, `getTarget` returns the actual composed target inside the shadow root, while `event.target` would be the shadow host. The original code was checking "did the user click the scrollbar itself vs. the thumb" — this still works because the thumb is a child of the scrollbar in the light DOM. No practical issue, but worth a comment.

3. **useCompositeRoot.ts** — The `getTarget` is used in `onFocus` and `onKeyDown` where the target is checked against `isNativeInput`. In shadow DOM, `composedPath()[0]` could return an element inside a shadow root that the composite root doesn't contain in its light DOM tree. The null check (`target == null`) is good, but this is a somewhat subtle behavioral change worth noting.

4. **Duplicate `getTarget` implementations** — `StoreInspector.tsx` duplicates `getTarget` inline. This is justified by package boundaries but could eventually be extracted to `@base-ui/utils` if more utils code needs it.

---

### Merge Readiness Score: **8.5 / 10**

| Category | Score | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness | 9/10 | All conversions are semantically sound. Minor subtlety around `getTarget` in composite root shadow DOM scenarios. |
| Completeness | 8/10 | Thorough sweep across 30 files. A few minor stragglers exist (FloatingPortal.tsx, `window.Image()`) but were pre-existing, not introduced by this PR. |
| Code quality | 9/10 | Clean extraction into `shadowDom.ts`, good re-export pattern, appropriate `currentTarget` usage. |
| Testing | 7/10 | No new tests added. Shadow DOM behavior is hard to test in JSDOM, but at least one Chromium test exercising a shadow DOM scenario would strengthen confidence. |
| Risk | Low | Changes are mechanical and well-scoped. The `markOthers` correction in commit 2 shows good self-review. |

**Recommendation:** Approve with the suggestion to add at least one integration test for a component inside a shadow root (Chromium env) to validate the `getTarget`/`contains`/`activeElement` utilities work end-to-end.
